name: 拾漂岗
Driftwood Rise
before: 荒滩高处一道岗子，每逢大潮，海上漂来的东西都搁在岗下：断桅、木桶、船板、鞋。一队雾海水兵在岗上设了卡，说舰队修船缺木头，凡是漂来的木料一律充公。拾漂的老瘸子不肯交，水兵就连他那条木头假腿也卸了，扛在肩上走。

A rise above the strand where, at every spring tide, whatever the sea brings in fetches up below: broken masts, barrels, planks, shoes. A squad of Fog Sea marines has set a checkpoint on top. The fleet needs timber for repairs, they say, so all drifted wood is forfeit. The old lame beachcomber won't hand his over, so the marines unstrap his wooden leg as well and march off with it on a shoulder.
after: 水兵被赶跑，老瘸子单腿蹦着把假腿抢了回来。他棚子里供着一块舱盖板，刻着「千里·六」。十年前九月初二清早，一个后生抱着这块板子漂上了滩，冻得嘴唇发紫，嘴里只念三个字：「一号泊。」

The marines are chased off and the old man hops after his leg on one foot and gets it back. In his shed, set up like a shrine, is a hatch cover carved 'Qianli Six'. Early on the second day of the ninth month, ten years ago, a young man washed up on the strand clinging to it, lips blue with cold, saying only three words over and over: 'Berth Number One.'

name: 煮盐场
The Salt Boilery
before: 滩头一片煮盐场，几十口铁锅架在灶上，海水熬得咕嘟咕嘟，白汽和雾搅在一起。盐场的主人葛三娘是个高颧骨的寡妇，嗓门比锅还响。今天一伙雾海跳帮手来「拉夫」，舰队缺人，见了男丁就套绳子。葛三娘抄起一把盐耙挡在灶前：「要拉人，先把我这锅盐熬干！」

A salt boilery on the strand, dozens of iron pans over fires, seawater bubbling down, the steam mixing with the fog. It belongs to Third Sister Ge, a high-cheekboned widow whose voice is louder than her pans. Today a gang of Fog Sea boarders has come press-ganging: the fleet is short of men, and any man they see gets a rope round him. Third Sister plants herself before the fires with a salt rake: 'You want my men, you boil this pan dry first!'
after: 跳帮手被打散，套走的盐丁都放了回来。葛三娘说那个漂上滩的后生叫阿舟，泉州人，在她这儿熬了一年盐，每回系船都在桩上刻个「一」。后来舰队来拉夫，他自己走上前报了名。「他说，要找千里号，就得跟着截它的人。」

The boarders are scattered and the roped men come home. The young man who washed up, Third Sister says, was called Azhou, from Quanzhou. He boiled salt for her for a year and carved a '1' on every post he tied a boat to. When the fleet came press-ganging, he stepped up and signed on of his own accord. 'He said if you want to find the Qianli, you follow the people sent to stop it.'

name: 刺青寮
The Tattoo Hut
before: 路边一间草寮，门口挂着一张画满花样的布：锚、鲤鱼、妈祖像、一只眼睛。寮里的刺青婆手稳，水手出海前都来刺一样东西，说是淹死了好认。一伙雾海弩手占着草寮，逼她给每人刺上营号，刺慢了就拿弩柄敲桌子。刺青婆眼神不好，已经把一个人的「七营」刺成了「七管」。

A grass hut by the road with a cloth of patterns hung at the door: anchors, carp, the goddess Mazu, a single eye. The tattoo granny inside has a steady hand, and sailors come to her before they ship out, so that if they drown they can be known. Fog Sea crossbowmen have taken over the hut and are making her ink each of them with his unit number, rapping the table with their crossbow stocks if she's slow. Her eyesight isn't good, and one man's 'Seventh Company' has already come out as 'Seventh Pipe'.
after: 弩手们捂着胳膊跑了。刺青婆翻出花样本，指着一页：一根系船柱，柱上一个「一」。「十年前一个泉州后生让我刺的，刺在左小臂上。他说他哥给他留着一个泊位，怕自己忘了，也怕人家认不出他。」

The crossbowmen run off clutching their arms. The granny opens her pattern book to one page: a mooring bollard with a '1' on it. 'A young man from Quanzhou had this done, ten years ago, on his left forearm. His brother was keeping a berth for him, he said. He was afraid he'd forget, and afraid no one would know him.'

name: 草人田
Scarecrow Field
before: 一片番薯地里插满了草人，戴斗笠，披蓑衣，在雾里一动不动。一队雾海水兵挨个拿枪捅草人，捅一个骂一句：舰上跑了个逃兵，有人说他就藏在这片地里。捅到第三十七个，草人「哎哟」了一声。

A sweet-potato field full of scarecrows in rain hats and straw capes, motionless in the fog. A squad of Fog Sea marines is jabbing each one with a spear and cursing: a deserter has run from the fleet, and someone says he's hiding in this field. At the thirty-seventh, the scarecrow says 'Ow.'
after: 水兵被赶跑，草人自己摘了斗笠：逃兵老钩。十年前那一夜他就在跳帮队里：千里号最后一条船忽然灭了灯，横着撞进舰队的阵里，前头五条趁乱溜了。「我们跳上去，船上只剩一个后生掌舵，见了我们，翻身就下了海。」

The marines are chased off and the scarecrow takes off its own hat: Old Hook, a deserter. That night ten years ago he was in the boarding party. The Qianli's last ship suddenly doused its lights and rammed broadside into the fleet's line, and the five ahead slipped away in the confusion. 'We jumped aboard and found just one young fellow at the helm. He saw us and went straight over the side.'

name: 军饼坊
The Hardtack Ovens
before: 大路边一排烤炉，本是村里人烤番薯饼的。一队雾海水兵把炉子全占了，逼村妇日夜烤军饼，一块饼硬得能钉钉子，烤好了一车车运去舰队。村里的孩子饿得啃炉灰，水兵却拿多出来的饼当枕头。

A row of ovens by the high road where the villagers used to bake sweet-potato cakes. A squad of Fog Sea marines has taken every one and keeps the village women baking hardtack day and night, biscuits hard enough to drive nails, carted off load by load to the fleet. The village children are hungry enough to gnaw the oven ash, while the marines use the spare biscuits as pillows.
after: 水兵被赶走，炉子又烤上了番薯饼，香甜味飘出半里地。坊里的老面头翻出舰队的领饼单，每月一张，有一行十年没变过：「镇雾号，号手阿舟，饼一份，不要芝麻。」阿舟还活着，在提督的旗舰上吹号。

With the marines gone the ovens bake sweet-potato cakes again, and the smell carries half a li. The old head baker digs out the fleet's biscuit orders, one sheet a month, and one line hasn't changed in ten years: 'Zhenwu. Bugler Azhou. One ration. No sesame.' Azhou is alive, blowing the horn on the admiral's flagship.
first: 炉房里抄出水兵囤的四十袋面粉、三百块军饼、两坛猪油，还有一只装满芝麻的布袋，上面写着「号手不吃，别浪费」。
In the oven house you find the marines' hoard: forty sacks of flour, three hundred biscuits, two crocks of lard, and a cloth bag full of sesame marked 'Bugler won't eat it. Don't waste it.'
pass: 每次路过，村妇们都塞给你们一摞刚出炉的番薯饼，软的，说「硬的留给舰队，软的给自己人」。
Every time you pass, the village women hand you a stack of sweet-potato cakes straight from the oven, the soft kind. 'The hard ones are for the fleet. The soft ones are for our own.'

name: 螺号营
Conch Horn Camp
before: 荒原上一座号营，营里天天呜呜地响：雾海水师在这里教新兵吹海螺、打鼓、摇铃。雾里看不见旗，全靠声音传令。营里的水兵、弩手、跳帮手见你们来了，几十只海螺一齐吹响，震得人耳朵嗡嗡，营门口的鹅吓得飞上了墙。

A signal camp on the moor that moans all day long: here the Fog Sea navy teaches recruits the conch, the drum and the bell, for in fog no one can see a flag and every order goes by sound. At the sight of you the camp's marines, crossbowmen and boarders blow dozens of conches at once, until your ears ring and the geese at the gate flap up onto the wall in fright.
after: 号营散了，海螺扔了一地。老号头说，阿舟是他教过最好的号手，一口气能吹半炷香，还会拿海螺吹泉州的南音。学成那天他只求了一件事：上旗舰。「他说提督的船站在最前头，千里号要是回来，头一个看见的就是那条船。」

The camp breaks up and conches litter the ground. Azhou, says the old horn-master, was the best he ever taught. He could hold a note for half a joss stick and play Quanzhou's nanyin songs on a conch. On the day he passed he asked for one thing only: the flagship. 'He said the admiral's ship stands at the very front. If the Qianli ever comes back, that ship sees it first.'

name: 苏拉竹楼
Sura's Bamboo House
before: 大路边一座竹楼，挂满了花花绿绿的南洋布。楼主是个黑皮肤的蛮商娘子苏拉，十年前跟船来做买卖，船被雾海水师扣在雾里，从此回不了家，只好在岸上开铺。一伙雾海弩手赖在楼下，天天收她「滞留钱」；她不交，弩手就拿箭把她的布一匹匹钉在墙上。

A bamboo house by the high road hung with bright South Seas cloth. It belongs to Sura, a dark-skinned trader from the southern isles who came on a ship to trade ten years ago. The Fog Sea navy held the ship in the fog and she has never got home since, so she opened a shop on shore. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen loafs below demanding a 'stranded fee' every day; when she won't pay, they pin her cloth to the wall bolt by bolt.
after: 弩手被打跑，苏拉把布一匹匹从墙上拔下来，佩服你们，开铺换货。她说舰上有个泉州号手，每年上岸都来买一沓南洋纸、一小瓶墨，「写信用的。可我从没见他寄过」。

The crossbowmen are driven off and Sura pulls her cloth down from the wall bolt by bolt. Impressed, she opens her shop to you. A Quanzhou bugler from the fleet, she says, comes ashore every year and buys a stack of southern paper and a little bottle of ink. 'For letters. But I've never once seen him send one.'

name: 望归石
Homecoming Rock
before: 荒原尽头一块大石头，像一只蹲着的狗，面朝大海。每天傍晚，葛三娘的女儿葛青都坐在石头上织网，织到天黑。一伙雾海弩手拿这块石头当靶子练箭，箭一支支钉在她身边，她头也不抬，梭子照样一来一回。

At the moor's far end sits a great rock shaped like a crouching dog, facing the sea. Every evening Ge Qing, Third Sister's daughter, sits on it netting until dark. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen uses the rock for target practice, bolts thudding in all around her, and she never looks up; her shuttle goes on, back and forth.
after: 弩手们被赶走，葛青才放下网。她和阿舟定过亲，他上船那天给她留了一根小木桩，刻着一个「一」：「我哥给我留一号泊，我给你留一个『一』。」他每年上岸一回，每回都说「快了」。这句「快了」，说了九年。

Only when the crossbowmen are gone does Ge Qing put down her net. She and Azhou were betrothed. The day he joined the ship he left her a little wooden post carved with a '1': 'My brother's keeping Berth One for me. I'm keeping a one for you.' He comes ashore once a year and every time he says, 'Soon.' He has been saying 'soon' for nine years.

name: 草船校场
The Turf Ship Ground
before: 一片大校场上，拿草皮垒了一条「船」，有桅有舱，跟真船一般大。雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手每天在这里练一件事：跳上草船，夺舵、灭灯、拿人。练了十年，跳得比猴还快。今天他们刚喊完号子，见你们来了，就拿你们当了靶子。

On a great parade ground stands a 'ship' built of stacked turf, masts and holds and all, as big as the real thing. Every day Fog Sea marines, crossbowmen and boarders drill one thing here: leap aboard the turf ship, seize the helm, douse the lights, take the crew. Ten years of it, and they jump faster than monkeys. They've just finished their drill chant when you arrive, and they make you the target.
after: 校场散了，你们爬上草船看了看：九个舱，舵在左舷，三根桅。可千里号是十三舱。操典第一页写着：「千里号形制，据号手阿舟口述。」老钩一拍大腿：「这小子！他进水师，是给千里号当内应去的！」

The parade ground empties and you climb up to look: nine holds, a helm on the port side, three masts. But the Qianli had thirteen holds. The drill book's first page says: 'Form of the Qianli, as described by Bugler Azhou.' Old Hook slaps his thigh. 'That boy! He joined the navy to work for the Qianli from the inside!'

name: 天妃筏
The Goddess Raft
before: 沼泽深处浮着一座竹筏搭的天妃庙，供着一尊黑脸妈祖，筏边系满了许愿的木牌，风一吹哗啦哗啦响。一队雾海水兵占了庙，说木牌上写的都是「私通千里号」的话，要一块块劈了烧火。庙祝是个哑巴老婆婆，抱着一捆木牌坐在神像脚下，谁靠近就拿拂尘抽谁。

Deep in the marsh floats a temple to the Heavenly Consort built on a bamboo raft, with a black-faced Mazu inside and the raft's edges hung with wooden vow tablets that clatter in the wind. A squad of Fog Sea marines has taken over the temple; the tablets, they say, are full of 'secret dealings with the Qianli', and they mean to split them all for firewood. The temple keeper, a mute old woman, sits at the goddess's feet hugging a bundle of tablets and whips anyone who comes near with her horsetail whisk.
after: 水兵被赶下筏，庙祝把木牌一块块挂了回去。最旧的一块是船主沈渡十年前挂的：「千里号六船过此，愿六船同归。」旁边一块新些，字歪歪扭扭：「五船过了。六号的人都在，只差我一个。阿舟。」

The marines are thrown off the raft and the keeper hangs the tablets back one by one. The oldest was hung by Shen Du, owner of the fleet, ten years ago: 'The Qianli's six ships passed here. May all six come home.' Beside it hangs a newer one in a crooked hand: 'Five ships got through. Number Six's crew are all with them. Only I am missing. Azhou.'

name: 验信所
The Letter Office
before: 荒原上一座军邮所，舰上的家书都从这里过，信要先拆开验过才许送。所里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手识字不多，验信全凭一条：凡有「千」字的，烧。今天他们刚烧了一封写着「千万保重」的，写信的老水兵在门口跳着脚骂娘。

A military post office on the moor, through which every letter home from the fleet must pass, opened and inspected before it goes. The office's marines, crossbowmen and boarders can't read much, so they inspect by one rule: any letter with the character qian in it gets burned. They have just burned one that said 'take a thousand cares', and the old marine who wrote it is hopping with rage at the door.
after: 所里的兵散了。烧剩的信堆在铁箱里，最底下一摞却一封没烧：每年一封，十封，收信人都是「泉州龙四海」，信里一个「千」字也没有，却一封也没寄出去。书办说：「提督吩咐过，号手的信，不烧，也不寄。」

The office's soldiers scatter. The unburned letters sit in an iron chest, and at the very bottom is a bundle untouched by fire: one a year, ten in all, each addressed to 'Long Sihai, Quanzhou', and not a single qian in any of them, yet not one ever sent. 'The admiral's orders,' says the clerk. 'The bugler's letters are neither burned nor sent.'

name: 黑帆坞
Black Sail Dock
before: 荒原尽头一条暗沟通着海，沟里泊着几条涂成黑色的船，岸上堆满水桶、腌肉、缆绳：这是海贼的补给坞。雾海水师只截挂灯的船，海贼从来不点灯，摸黑进出，比谁都自在。坞里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手都是海贼花钱雇来的逃兵，身上还穿着水师的号衣。

At the moor's end a hidden channel runs to the sea, with a few black-painted ships moored in it and the bank piled with water casks, salt meat and cable: a pirates' supply dock. The Fog Sea navy stops only ships that show lights, and pirates never light a lamp, slipping in and out in the dark more freely than anyone. The marines, crossbowmen and boarders on guard are deserters the pirates pay, still wearing navy uniforms.
after: 这一回的海贼被赶下了海，补给烧了一半。老钩说，只要水师还只截有灯的船，黑船就会一条接一条地来，这座坞过不了几天又会塞满。坞墙上刻着一行字：「谢提督，截灯不截人。」刻字的人显然很得意。

This lot of pirates is driven into the sea and half the stores are burned. As long as the navy stops only lit ships, says Old Hook, the black ships will keep coming one after another, and in a few days the dock will be full again. Someone has carved a line on the dock wall: 'Thank you, Admiral, for stopping lights and not men.' Whoever carved it was clearly pleased with himself.

name: 金柑园
Kumquat Orchard
before: 坡上一片金柑园，小金柑一串串挂在枝头，在雾里黄得发亮。一伙雾海弩手守着园子，说金柑全归舰队，一颗也不许卖。园主老韦急得直搓手：柑子再不摘就要烂在树上，可弩手只许摘，不许运，因为舰队的船还没来取。

A kumquat orchard on the slope, little fruits hanging in clusters, glowing gold in the fog. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen guards it: every kumquat belongs to the fleet and not one may be sold. Old Wei the grower wrings his hands. Unpicked, the fruit will rot on the trees, but the crossbowmen let him pick and not haul, because the fleet's boat hasn't come to collect.
after: 弩手们被赶跑，老韦把金柑装满了几十只筐。他说舰上十年没靠过港，吃不上鲜果，好些人牙龈出血、牙齿松动，全靠这些柑子。每年春天，旗舰的号手都上岸来挑一筐最酸的：「他说船上牙不好的人多，酸的管用。」

The crossbowmen are chased off and Old Wei fills dozens of baskets. The fleet hasn't made port in ten years, he says, and without fresh fruit the men's gums bleed and their teeth work loose; these kumquats keep them going. Every spring the flagship's bugler comes ashore and picks a basket of the sourest. 'Lots of bad teeth aboard, he says. The sour ones do the job.'

name: 鸡鸣墩
Cockcrow Mound
before: 荒原上一座土墩，墩上养着几十只大公鸡。雾岸的渔家都知道：雾里分不清早晚，听鸡叫才知道天亮了，海上的船听着鸡叫也认得回家的方向。一伙雾海弩手抢鸡，说要送去舰上，抓不住的就射。鸡毛满天飞，养鸡的老汉追着自己的鸡哭。

An earth mound on the moor where dozens of big roosters are kept. Every fisher family on the Fog Coast knows that in fog you can't tell morning from evening, so you wait for the cocks to tell you it's dawn, and boats out at sea find their way home by the crowing. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen is grabbing the roosters for the fleet and shooting the ones they can't catch. Feathers fill the air, and the old poultryman chases his birds in tears.
after: 弩手被赶走，公鸡们骂骂咧咧回了墩子。老汉说，旗舰上那只最响的芦花鸡就是他的，是号手阿舟亲手抱上船的：「他说船上的人在雾里漂久了，连过了几天都记不清，得有只鸡替他们数日子。」

With the crossbowmen gone, the roosters stalk back to the mound grumbling. The loudest bird on the flagship, the old man says, a speckled cock, is one of his, carried aboard in Azhou the bugler's own arms. 'He said the men have drifted in the fog so long they can't even keep track of the days. They need a rooster to count them.'

name: 困班车
The Stranded Circus
before: 荒原上停着几辆大篷车，车篷上画着狮子和火圈：一个南洋来的马戏班子，十年前要过海，船被扣在雾里，就困在了这片荒原。一队雾海水兵把篷车围住，逼他们每夜演一场，演砸了不给饭吃。班里的老熊已经学会帮着翻番薯地，走钢丝的姑娘在绳上睡觉。

A few covered wagons stand on the moor, their canvas painted with lions and rings of fire: a South Seas circus that tried to cross the sea ten years ago, had its ship held in the fog, and has been stuck on this moor ever since. A squad of Fog Sea marines surrounds the wagons, making them put on a show every night and docking their supper if it flops. The troupe's old bear has learned to dig the sweet-potato beds, and the tightrope girl sleeps on her rope.
after: 水兵被赶走，班主请你们看了一场不收钱的戏。他说去年水师过年，叫他们上旗舰演过一回，台下有个吹海螺的年轻人，趁乱塞给他一张纸条：「告诉煮盐的三娘，我找到他们去的路了。」班主一直没敢去送。

The marines are driven off and the ringmaster gives you a show for free. Last New Year, he says, the navy had them perform aboard the flagship, and in the crowd a young conch-blower slipped him a note in the confusion: 'Tell Third Sister at the salt pans I've found the way they went.' The ringmaster never dared deliver it.

name: 抄图斋
The Chart Copier's
before: 一座小书斋，门口挂着「代抄海图」的幌子，斋主是个近视的老秀才，替舰队抄海图，一张图抄三份，一份不许多。一伙雾海弩手守在门口，抄完一张收一张，连画坏的草稿也要拿去烧。老秀才趁人不注意，把一张草稿塞进了砚台底下。

A little study with a 'Charts Copied' banner at the door, kept by a short-sighted old scholar who copies charts for the fleet: three copies of each, not one more. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen stands at the door collecting each chart as it's done and burning even his spoiled drafts. When no one is looking, the old scholar slips one draft under his inkstone.
after: 弩手被赶走，老秀才从砚台底下抽出那张草稿：是旗舰号手去年拿来请他誊的一张私图，雾海东南角画着一条细线，线的尽头没画海，画了几座楼台，旁注：「八月十八，雾开一线，东南有城。千里号往此去。」

With the crossbowmen gone the old scholar draws the draft from under his inkstone: a private chart the flagship's bugler brought him to copy last year. A thin line runs into the south-east corner of the Sea of Fog, and where it ends he drew no sea but towers and terraces, with a note: 'Eighteenth of the eighth month. The fog opens a crack. A city in the south-east. The Qianli went this way.'

name: 六号搁浅处
Where Number Six Lies
before: 荒原尽头的高地上搁着一条大船，离海足有半里，是十年前一场风暴潮把它推上来的。船头漆着「千里·六」，船舷被撞出一个大洞，已经拿新木板补了一半。雾海水师把它当战利品，派了最精的水兵、弩手、跳帮手守着，营旗插在船头，谁也不许靠近。

On the high ground at the moor's end lies a great ship, half a li from the sea, where a storm surge pushed it ten years ago. 'Qianli Six' is painted on its bow. A huge hole is stove in its side, and half of it has been patched with new planks. The Fog Sea navy keeps it as a war prize, guarded by its finest marines, crossbowmen and boarders, a company flag planted on the bow, and no one may approach.
after: 守兵败了。舱里收拾得干干净净，最小的那张铺位上刻满了「正」字，一天一笔，刻了十年。船舷的破洞是有人一年年补的，补到了一半。铺头压着一张纸：「等提督撤了令，我就开六号回泉州，靠一号泊。」字是阿舟的。

The guards are beaten. Inside, the ship is swept clean, and the smallest bunk is carved all over with tally marks, a stroke a day for ten years. Someone has been patching the hole in the side, year by year, and is halfway done. Under the bunk's pillow end lies a sheet of paper: 'When the admiral lifts his order, I'll sail Number Six home to Quanzhou and moor at Berth One.' The hand is Azhou's.

name: 蛎灰窑
Oyster-Lime Kiln
before: 荒原上冒着白烟，是一座烧牡蛎壳的灰窑，壳烧成灰，掺上桐油就是补船缝的油灰。一队雾海水兵把窑占了，烧出来的灰全运去舰队，窑户们一袋也留不下，自家屋顶漏雨都补不上。窑主老灶脸上糊满了白灰，像戏台上的白脸奸臣。

White smoke rises from the moor: a kiln that burns oyster shells to lime, which mixed with tung oil makes the putty that seals a ship's seams. A squad of Fog Sea marines has seized it and ships every bag to the fleet, leaving the kiln families none, not even enough to stop their own roofs leaking. Old Zao the kiln master is plastered white with lime, like the villain's painted face in an opera.
after: 水兵被赶走，窑户们头一回给自家屋顶补上了灰。老灶说，十年来每次舰队的人上岸，旗舰的号手都要单买两袋灰，背着往西南的高地去。「我们不问他补什么。补船的人，心里都有一条船。」

With the marines gone, the kiln families patch their own roofs for the first time. For ten years, says Old Zao, whenever fleet men came ashore, the flagship's bugler bought two bags of lime of his own and carried them off toward the high ground in the south-west. 'We never asked what he was patching. Every man who patches ships has a ship in his heart.'
first: 窑里抄出水兵囤的六十袋蛎灰、三桶桐油、一筐晒干的海蛎，还有一本账簿，号手那一栏写着「自付，不入公账」。

In the kiln you find the marines' hoard: sixty bags of oyster lime, three kegs of tung oil, a basket of dried oysters, and a ledger whose column for the bugler reads 'Paid himself. Not on the public account.'
pass: 每次路过，窑户们都往车上搬两袋新灰，再煮一锅海蛎粥，说「车坏了船漏了，都拿它补」。
Every time you pass, the kiln families load two bags of fresh lime onto your carts and cook a pot of oyster congee. 'Broken cart or leaking boat, this'll patch it.'

name: 挂包门
The Door with the Bundle
before: 荒原边一户人家，门楣上挂着一只褪色的布包，十年没人碰过。老主人从前是跑泉州的船家，十年前最后一趟回来，带了一封托他捎给「雾海水师阿舟」的信，可舰队不许民船靠近，信就一直挂在门上。一伙雾海弩手听说布包里有「泉州来的密信」，正搭梯子要摘。

A house on the moor's edge with a faded cloth bundle hanging from its lintel, untouched for ten years. Its old owner once sailed the Quanzhou run, and on his last trip home ten years ago he brought a letter he'd been asked to deliver to 'Azhou, Fog Sea Navy'. But the fleet lets no civilian boat come near, so the letter has hung over the door ever since. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has heard the bundle holds 'a secret letter from Quanzhou' and is propping a ladder to take it down.
after: 弩手被赶跑，老船家颤着手把布包交给你们。信是龙老太托人写的，十年前寄出：「阿舟，娘熬了面线糊，回来吃。你哥嘴硬，泊位他留着。」信封里还夹着一枚铜钱，给他买糖的。信迟到了十年，那枚铜钱还亮着。

The crossbowmen are chased off and the old boatman hands you the bundle with shaking hands. The letter was written for old Mrs Long, sent ten years ago: 'Azhou, Mother has made noodle porridge. Come home and eat. Your brother talks tough, but he's keeping the berth.' Tucked in the envelope is a copper coin, for him to buy sweets. The letter is ten years late, and the coin still shines.

name: 送饷湾
Supply Boat Cove
before: 荒原边的小湾里停着一条送饷的快艇，每月一回，把岸上的米、柑子、信送去旗舰。一伙雾海弩手守着艇，说这个月不送了：岸营报来，有一条挂千字灯的船进了雾海，提督下令封海。葛三娘和葛青提着一篮东西站在湾边，不肯走。

In a little cove on the moor's edge waits the fast supply boat that once a month carries rice, kumquats and letters from shore out to the flagship. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen guards it: no run this month. The shore forts report a ship with Qian lanterns has entered the Sea of Fog, and the admiral has closed the sea. Third Sister Ge and Ge Qing stand at the water's edge with a basket and won't leave.
after: 弩手们被打散，艇夫答应照常开船。葛青把那根刻着「一」的小木桩放进篮子，龙老太的信压在最上面。艇夫说旗舰停在东南的岛群里，「号手每年八月廿六都站在船头，往西吹一夜海螺」。

The crossbowmen are scattered and the boatman agrees to sail as usual. Ge Qing puts the little post carved with a '1' in the basket and lays old Mrs Long's letter on top. The flagship lies among the islands to the south-east, the boatman says. 'Every twenty-sixth of the eighth month the bugler stands in the bow and blows his conch westward all night long.'

name: 换防路口
The Relief Crossroads
before: 去海边的路口驻着一队雾海水兵，刚从东边的海上集换防回来，一路走一路嚷嚷：「千里号回来了！集上的人都瞧见了，三百盏灯！」领头的什长急着去报提督，要把这条路封了，谁也不许往东走。

A squad of Fog Sea marines holds the crossroads on the way to the sea, just back from garrison duty at the floating market in the east and shouting all the way: 'The Qianli's back! Everyone at the market saw it, three hundred lanterns!' Their sergeant is in a hurry to tell the admiral and wants the road closed so no one goes east.
after: 水兵被打散，什长这才弄明白，集上看见的「千里号」就是你们的后千里。他挠着头说，舰上听见这个消息，最高兴的是号手，最难办的是提督：「令上写的是千里号，见了就截。他截还是不截？」

The marines are scattered and the sergeant finally understands that the 'Qianli' the market saw was your Houqianli. He scratches his head. When the fleet hears the news, the happiest man aboard will be the bugler and the one in the hardest spot will be the admiral. 'The order says the Qianli, stop it on sight. So does he stop you or not?'

name: 一字桩
The Number-One Post
before: 西南的岬角上孤零零立着一根系船桩，桩顶刻着「一」，被缆绳磨得发亮。阿舟每回上岸，都把小艇系在这根桩上。如今桩边扎着一座雾海水师的哨营，水兵、弩手、跳帮手都有，奉的是新到的令：「凡有人来认此桩，拿下，押送旗舰。」

On the south-western headland stands a lone mooring post with a '1' carved on top, worn shiny by ropes. Every time Azhou came ashore, he tied his skiff to it. Now a Fog Sea outpost camps beside it, marines, crossbowmen and boarders, under a fresh order: 'Anyone who comes asking after this post is to be seized and sent to the flagship.'
after: 哨营被打散。桩脚下埋着一只油布匣，装着一张手画的海图和一封信：「哥，我找到他们去的地方了，雾尽头有一座楼。提督不撤令，我不能走；我走了，谁替他们看着这片海？」葛青把小木桩插在旁边，一大一小并排站着。

The outpost is scattered. Buried at the foot of the post is an oilcloth box holding a hand-drawn chart and a letter: 'Brother, I've found where they went. At the end of the fog there's a tower. While the admiral's order stands I can't leave. If I left, who would watch this sea for them?' Ge Qing plants her little post beside it, the big one and the small one standing together.

name: 雾栈渡
Fog Boardwalk Ferry
before: 沼泽和海交界的地方，一排高脚木屋连成长长的栈道，栈道尽头是渡口。渡夫老篙远远望见后千里桅上的灯笼，扔下竹篙就往栈道上跑，一路敲着各家的门喊：「千里号回来了！千里号回来了！」一队雾海水兵追上来，把他按在栈板上，说他妖言惑众。

Where marsh meets sea, a row of stilt houses is joined by a long boardwalk with a ferry landing at its end. Old Pole the ferryman sees the lanterns on Houqianli's masts from far off, drops his pole and runs down the boardwalk, banging on every door: 'The Qianli's back! The Qianli's back!' A squad of Fog Sea marines comes after him and pins him to the planks for spreading wild rumours.
after: 水兵被赶下栈道。老篙盯着你们的灯笼看了半天，有点失望，又不死心。他撑船送你们去海上集，一路上说：千里号当年在集上赊了一船货，还带走了集上最好的领港鲍老针。「满集的人等了十年，等它回来结账，也等老针。」

The marines are pushed off the boardwalk. Old Pole stares at your lanterns a long time, a little disappointed and not yet ready to give up. He poles you to the floating market, telling you on the way that the Qianli took a shipload of goods on credit there, and took the market's best pilot too, Bao Laozhen. 'The whole market's waited ten years for it to come back and settle up. And for Old Needle.'

name: 八哥茶亭
The Mynah's Teahouse
before: 路边一座茶亭，梁上挂着个鸟笼，笼里一只八哥，见人就喊：「欠钱！欠钱！」茶亭掌柜是海上集的讨债人，八哥是他养的帮手。一伙雾海弩手在亭里喝茶不给钱，八哥冲着他们喊了半天「提督欠饷！提督欠饷！」，弩手们恼了，要拧它的脖子。

A roadside teahouse with a cage hanging from the beam, and in the cage a mynah that shouts at everyone, 'Pay up! Pay up!' The owner is the floating market's debt collector and the bird is his assistant. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has been drinking without paying, and the mynah has spent the afternoon screaming 'Admiral owes wages! Admiral owes wages!' at them. Now they've lost their temper and want to wring its neck.
after: 弩手们被赶走，八哥抖抖毛，瞅了一眼你们的灯笼，忽然换了一套词：「千里号！牛油三百斤！铜锣六十面！领港一个！」掌柜红了脸：那是集上记了十年的千里号赊账，八哥听多了，背熟了。它只对挂灯的船背这一段。

With the crossbowmen gone, the mynah shakes out its feathers, eyes your lanterns, and changes its tune: 'Qianli! Three hundred jin of tallow! Sixty bronze gongs! One pilot!' The owner goes red. That's the Qianli's tab, kept at the market for ten years; the bird heard it so often it learned it by heart. It recites that one only to ships with lanterns.

name: 百针屋
House of a Hundred Needles
before: 一间小屋的四壁挂满了罗盘，大大小小上百只，指针各指各的，没有两只朝同一个方向。屋主鲍婶是领港鲍老针的老伴。一伙雾海弩手闯进来抢罗盘，说舰队的船一到黑沙嘴就迷路，要好针。鲍婶坐在门槛上剥花生：「拿吧，这一屋子针，没一根准的。」

The walls of a small house are covered in compasses, more than a hundred large and small, every needle pointing its own way, no two alike. The house belongs to Auntie Bao, wife of the pilot Bao Laozhen. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen bursts in to seize the compasses: the fleet's ships get lost every time they reach the Black Sand Spit, and they want good needles. Auntie Bao sits on the doorstep shelling peanuts. 'Take them. There isn't an honest needle in the house.'
after: 弩手们抱着罗盘跑了几步，又扔了回来。鲍婶说老针一辈子不信针：「这片海底下有铁石，针到了那儿就撒谎。」他听浪、摸水，凭耳朵和手领船。千里号付了他一半工钱，说好回来付另一半；他说一个月就回。那是十年前。

The crossbowmen run a few steps with the compasses and throw them back. Old Needle, says Auntie Bao, never trusted a needle in his life. 'There's iron-stone under this sea, and when a needle gets there it lies.' He piloted by ear and by hand, listening to the surf, feeling the water. The Qianli paid him half his fee, the rest on the way back, and he said he'd be home in a month. That was ten years ago.

name: 海上集
The Floating Market
before: 沼泽边上几百条船并排拴着，船挨船，板接板，铺成一大片水上集市，卖鱼的、卖布的、卖药的、卖罗盘的，吵得像开了锅。后千里的灯笼一露头，整个集市忽然静了，接着有人哭，有人笑，有人敲锣：「千里号回来了！」几十个人捧着账本往前挤。可挤在最前头的是一队雾海水兵，他们来收「水师饷」，正好撞上。

Hundreds of boats are lashed side by side at the marsh's edge, hull against hull, plank to plank, into one great market on the water: fish, cloth, medicine, compasses, the noise of a pot on the boil. The moment Houqianli's lanterns show, the whole market falls silent. Then someone weeps, someone laughs, someone bangs a gong: 'The Qianli's come back!' Dozens push forward clutching account books. But at the very front is a squad of Fog Sea marines who came to collect the 'navy levy' and walked straight into it.
after: 水兵被赶下船板，集上的人围上来，看清了你们船尾的字：后千里。愣了一会儿，有人先笑出声：「后来的也算！」金子换木料的买卖重新做了起来，搁了十年的账本一本本摊开。集老拿出千里号的赊条：「牛油三百斤，铜锣六十面，领港鲍老针一人。回程付清。」他把赊条交给你们：「后来的，替我们看看，它们到底去了哪儿。」

The marines are driven off the planks and the market crowds round and reads the name on your stern: Houqianli, After-Qianli. For a moment no one speaks. Then someone laughs first: 'Coming after counts!' Gold for timber, the trade starts up again, and ten years of account books open one by one. The market elder brings out the Qianli's credit note: 'Tallow, three hundred jin. Bronze gongs, sixty. Pilot Bao Laozhen, one. To be paid in full on the return voyage.' He gives the note to you. 'You who came after: find out for us where they went.'

name: 抽饷寨
The Levy Stockade
before: 集市边一座水寨，是雾海水师的抽饷营，集上每卖一条鱼，营里抽一片鳞。营里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手样样都有，饷一车车往舰队运。营门口立着块牌子：「奉令就市取给。」牌子底下蹲着几个卖鱼的老太太，一边骂，一边数自己还剩几片鳞。

A stockade on the water by the market, the Fog Sea navy's levy post: for every fish sold, it takes a scale. Marines, crossbowmen, boarders, it has them all, and the takings go off to the fleet by the cartload. A board at the gate reads 'By order, supplies to be drawn from the market.' Under it squat a few old fishwives, cursing and counting how many scales they've got left.
after: 抽饷寨被打散，账本摊了一桌：朝廷十年没发过一文饷，舰队全靠这座寨子吃饭。最后几页记着：「七月，抽米三百石，送镇雾号。号手又来问：鲍老针那条空舢板里的银子，可还在库里？」

The stockade is broken up and its ledgers cover a table. The court hasn't paid the fleet a copper in ten years; this stockade is what keeps it fed. The last pages read: 'Seventh month: three hundred shi of rice levied, sent to the Zhenwu. The bugler came asking again whether the silver from Bao Laozhen's empty skiff is still in the store.'

name: 高跷滩
Stilt Flats
before: 沼泽里的滩民不坐船，踩高跷，一步跨过一条水沟，远远看去像一群白鹭。一伙雾海跳帮手也学着踩，踩得东倒西歪，倒是很会抢：从高处一钩，就把滩民背篓里的蟹钩走。滩上有个十二岁的男孩踩得最高最稳，跳帮手追了他一早上，连根毛都没捞着。

The marsh folk don't use boats; they walk on stilts, stepping over a channel in a stride, like a flock of egrets from far off. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken up stilts too, tottering all over, but they're good at stealing: one hook from up high and a crab is gone from a basket. One boy of twelve walks tallest and steadiest of all, and the boarders have chased him all morning without catching a hair of him.
after: 跳帮手们摔进了泥里。那男孩从高跷上一跃而下，自报家门：鲍小桨，鲍老针的孙子。爷爷教过他，雾里走路不能靠看，要靠听：「浪打在礁上是噗，打在沙上是沙沙，打在船上是咚。」他要跟你们走，去找爷爷。

The boarders topple into the mud. The boy leaps down from his stilts and introduces himself: Bao Xiaojiang, Old Needle's grandson. Grandpa taught him that in fog you don't walk by looking but by listening. 'Surf on rock goes pff. On sand it goes shhh. On a hull it goes boom.' He wants to come with you and find his grandfather.

name: 盲舟塾
The Blind Pilots' School
before: 荒原上一间草堂，堂里坐着七八个盲人，都是雾海上数一数二的领港，眼睛看不见，雾里反倒比明眼人稳。一伙雾海跳帮手要把他们全抓去舰上领船：舰队这几年在雾里撞礁撞得太多了。老塾师拄着竹竿挡在门口，侧着耳朵：「来了九个，左边那个腿瘸。」

A thatched hall on the moor where seven or eight blind men sit, among the best pilots on the Sea of Fog; they can't see, and so in fog they are steadier than the sighted. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has come to drag them all off to pilot the fleet, which has struck far too many rocks in the fog these last years. The old schoolmaster blocks the door with his bamboo cane, head cocked: 'Nine of you. The one on the left limps.'
after: 跳帮手们败了。老塾师说雾里认路靠喊：冲雾里喊一声，回声来得快，是崖；来得慢，是岛；没有回声，是开阔海。鲍老针是他的师弟，「他喊一嗓子，听得出前头有几座岛」。小桨扯着嗓子喊了一声，雾里什么也没回来。

The boarders are beaten. In fog, says the old master, you find your way by shouting. Call into the fog: if the echo comes back fast, it's a cliff; slow, an island; none at all, open sea. Bao Laozhen was his junior in the craft. 'One shout and he could tell you how many islands lay ahead.' Xiaojiang shouts at the top of his lungs. Nothing comes back out of the fog.

name: 记雾楼
The Fog Recorder's Loft
before: 一座小楼，楼上住着个画雾的老头，每天画一张雾图：雾从哪边来、有多厚、哪一片薄，十几年画了满满一屋子。一伙雾海跳帮手要把这些图全烧了，说「雾图就是海图，提督不许流出去」。老头被揪着胡子，还在跟他们争：「雾图不是海图！雾明天就变！」

In the loft of a small building lives an old man who draws the fog: one chart a day, where it came from, how thick, which patch thin. More than ten years of them fill the room. A gang of Fog Sea boarders means to burn them all. 'A fog chart is a sea chart, and the admiral won't have them getting out.' With his beard in their fists the old man is still arguing: 'A fog chart is not a sea chart! Fog changes by tomorrow!'
after: 跳帮手被赶走，雾图抢回了大半。老头翻出十年前八月的一张：一片浓雾中间，有人用朱笔添了一条细线，旁注「水暖处雾薄」，是鲍老针的笔迹。一线暖水穿过冷海，上面的雾就淡些，千里号是贴着这条暖水走的。

The boarders are driven off and most of the charts are saved. The old man finds one from the eighth month ten years ago: in the middle of thick fog someone has added a thin line in red, with a note, 'Thin fog where the water's warm', in Bao Laozhen's hand. Where a thread of warm water runs through the cold sea, the fog above it is thinner, and the Qianli followed that warm thread.

name: 捞雾拍卖
Fog Salvage Auction
before: 集市边一座大棚，雾海水兵在这里拍卖从雾里捞上来的东西：一只鞋、半张帆、一口没主的箱子，价高者得。今天的压轴货是一面铜锣，水兵敲了一下，锣声嗡嗡地传出去老远。台下的人一听这声音就不叫价了，有个老头站起来：「这是千里号的锣。」

In a big shed by the market, Fog Sea marines auction off whatever's been fished out of the fog: a shoe, half a sail, an ownerless chest, to the highest bidder. Today's final lot is a bronze gong. A marine strikes it once and the boom rolls out a long way. At the sound, the bidding stops, and an old man stands up: 'That's the Qianli's gong.'
after: 水兵被赶跑，铜锣还给了海上集。锣背刻着「千里·三」，锣槌上缠着鲍老针打的结。老头说那一夜雾里一直有锣声，六条船一船一声，一轮一轮地报，报的是「我在」。报着报着，就少了一声。

The marines are chased off and the gong goes back to the market. 'Qianli Three' is carved on its back, and Bao Laozhen's knot is wound round the striker. That night, the old man says, gongs sounded in the fog the whole time, one stroke per ship, six ships, round after round, each one saying 'I'm here.' Then, partway through, one stroke went missing.

name: 芦棚藏舟
The Boat in the Reed Shed
before: 芦苇棚里藏着一条小船，船头尖尖，船身漆成雾一样的灰白，叫「针」，是鲍老针的船。鲍小桨想把它推下水，自己去东边找爷爷。一伙雾海弩手听见动静，围住棚子要把船烧了：「舰上有令，雾海里不许多一条船。」小桨张开胳膊挡在船头。

Hidden in a reed shed is a small boat with a sharp bow, painted the grey-white of fog. It's called Needle, and it was Bao Laozhen's. Bao Xiaojiang wants to push it into the water and go east alone to find his grandfather. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen hears the noise and surrounds the shed to burn the boat: 'Fleet's orders. Not one more boat on the Sea of Fog.' Xiaojiang spreads his arms in front of the bow.
after: 弩手们被赶跑，船保住了。鲍婶赶来，没骂孙子，只往船舱里塞了一包干粮：「你爷爷当年也是这么走的。」说定了：「针」拴在后千里船尾一起走，小桨坐在后千里的船头听浪。

The crossbowmen are driven off and the boat is saved. Auntie Bao arrives and doesn't scold her grandson; she just tucks a parcel of food into the boat. 'Your grandpa left just like this.' It's settled: Needle will be towed behind Houqianli, and Xiaojiang will sit in Houqianli's bow and listen to the surf.
